extraInstructions: IMPORTANT: You MUST import and use BOTH audioManager AND speechManager. Import speechManager from '../../../lib/sim-engine/speech'. Use audioManager.play() for sound effects (valid: pickup, drop-correct, drop-wrong, tap, success, error, celebration, hint). Use speechManager.speak() for spoken teaching slide narration, challenge questions, correct/incorrect feedback, and hints. The game must teach: (1) Producers and consumers — Producers: make their own food using sunlight (photosynthesis). Examples: green plants, grass, trees, algae. Consumers: cannot make food, eat other organisms. Herbivores eat plants (deer, rabbit, cow). Carnivores eat other animals (tiger, lion, eagle). Omnivores eat both plants and animals (human, bear, crow). (2) Food chains — shows who eats whom. Always starts with a producer (plant), then herbivore, then carnivore. Arrows show energy flow: Grass -> Deer -> Tiger means energy passes from grass to deer to tiger. The sun is the ultimate energy source. (3) Decomposers and scavengers — Decomposers: break down dead plants and animals into simple substances that enrich soil. Examples: mushrooms, bacteria, earthworms. Scavengers: eat dead animals but do not break them down into soil nutrients. Examples: vulture, crow, hyena. Both help clean the environment. (4) Degradable and non-degradable waste — Deggradable: can be broken down naturally by decomposers. Examples: food scraps, vegetable peels, banana peel, paper, dry leaves, cloth. Non-degradable: cannot be broken down naturally, last for hundreds of years. Examples: plastic, glass, metal, synthetic materials. Degradable waste goes to compost, non-degradable goes to recycling. Misconceptions: 'decomposers and scavengers are the same' (WRONG — decomposers break down dead matter into soil nutrients; scavengers eat dead animals but do not break them into nutrients), 'food chains can start with any animal' (WRONG — food chains always start with a PRODUCER because only producers can make food from sunlight), 'all waste is the same' (WRONG — degradable waste breaks down naturally; non-degradable waste like plastic stays for hundreds of years), 'plastic is degradable because it gets old' (WRONG — plastic does not decompose; it only breaks into smaller pieces called microplastics), 'vultures are decomposers' (WRONG — vultures are scavengers; they eat dead animals but bacteria and fungi are the actual decomposers).
